title: background-variance-workload-synthesizer-and-aggregation-pipeline
author: Priya Shah
release_notes: Adds a background variance workload synthesizer and a downstream aggregator/reporting pipeline. New CSV/heatmap exporters and CI integration for percentile drift detection. No breaking changes to public runner API.
description: Motivation: current benchmark suites capture steady-state latency/throughput but miss background variance patterns that surface under mixed traffic (cold prefixes, sequence length spikes, intermittent small-batch noise). This PR introduces a synthetic workload generator (bg-var-synth) that composes steady-state drivers with controlled burst/noise processes to produce representative variance envelopes, and an aggregation pipeline (bg-agg) that computes time-windowed profiles, percentile heatmaps, and drift flags for CI. Changes: 1) New workload synthesizer library under benchmarks/synth/bg_var_synth.py with configurable modules: base_load, poisson_spikes, sporadic_small_batches, seq_length_jitter. 2) Runner extension for distributed scheduling (bench_runner supports --bg-synth-profile). 3) Aggregator service benchmarks/aggregator/ that ingests raw run traces and emits JSON summaries and CSV exports, plus a new heatmap PNG exporter for quick visual diffs. 4) CI integration: a new GH action workflow .github/workflows/benchmark-bg-var.yml that runs a short sampled profile on PRs and uploads artifacts to the build server; percentile regression check (p95/p99) can block merges if thresholds exceeded. 5) Profiling baseline: a small baseline dataset under benchmarks/baselines/bg_var_baseline.v1 to anchor drift alerts. 6) Docs: README and usage examples in benchmarks/docs/bg_var.md. Backwards compatibility: runner CLI flags are additive; existing benchmark definitions unaffected. Testing: unit tests for synthesizer stochastic seeds to ensure deterministic replay (benchmarks/tests/test_bg_var_synth.py), end-to-end integration test that runs on a trimmed config in CI and asserts aggregator outputs match baseline within tolerance. Performance notes: local end-to-end sample produced expected 3-8% p95 uplift during spike windows and exposed a scheduling hot path that was optimized in this PR. Related tickets: ENG-9812 design doc, SUP-3421 customer incident that motivated noise modeling. Checklist: - [x] Synthesizer implementation and unit tests - [x] Aggregator pipeline and exporters - [x] CI workflow and artifact upload - [x] Documentation and quickstart - [x] Added baseline artifacts - [x] Reviewer approvals and perf validation

review_comments: Daniel Kim (2026-02-19): Nice approach. Two asks: (1) please parametrize the default spike lambda to be explicit in config, and (2) add a short note about how this interacts with KV cache warmup. The aggregator code looks good but add a test for the heatmap colormap stability.

Priya Shah (2026-02-20): Addressed both comments. Default spike lambda moved to configs and documented; KV warmup behavior explained in bg_var.md and runner now optionally delays synthetic spikes until cache_warmup_seconds if provided.

Marta Alvarez (2026-02-21): Found a race in aggregator when multiple runner shards upload simultaneously; suggested a rename and a lock around the partial-merge step. Also requested an e2e CI run artifact for validation.
Priya Shah (2026-02-22): Fixed race by making partial merges atomic using temp files + rename; added e2e sample artifact to the workflow. Pushed updated tests and CI config.
Ethan Zhou (2026-02-24): CI artifacts look clean; p95 regressions for a known noisy config are within expected thresholds. Approving review.
Marta Alvarez (2026-02-24): Approving after verification of atomic merge logs and heatmap stability tests.

CI will start running a sampled profile on PRs; expect additional artifact uploads and a new dashboard for percentile heatmaps.
